## Correctness problem

The diff adds a new `provenance` object to the **TypeScript schema mirror** `packages/spec/src/schema.ts:228-238`, but does not update the **packaged JSON Schema artifact** `packages/spec/schema/v1.json`, which is a separate, checked-in file.

This matters because the runtime validator does not use `workspaceJsonSchema` from `schema.ts` at all. `packages/spec/src/index.ts:37-42` loads and compiles `../schema/v1.json` from disk — the comment there states explicitly: *"The runtime validator consumes the schema artifact that is published with the package, rather than the authoring-time TypeScript mirror."* I confirmed `schema/v1.json` (tail read) still ends with `health` as the last top-level property and has no `provenance` key, and the top-level schema keeps `additionalProperties: false` (mirrored at `packages/spec/src/schema.ts:7`, and asserted by test at `packages/spec/src/index.test.ts:331-333`).

Consequence: any document that actually includes a `provenance` field will be **rejected** by `validate()`/`validateV4()` at runtime (additional-property violation against the strict top-level schema in `v1.json`), even though the diff's intent — and the exported `workspaceJsonSchema` TS constant — says `provenance` is a valid optional field. The two schema sources are now out of sync ("split-brain").

This is not just a theoretical risk: the repo has an explicit regression test guarding exactly this invariant, `packages/spec/src/index.test.ts:324-329` ("workspaceJsonSchema top-level property keys match schema/v1.json"), which diffs `Object.keys(workspaceJsonSchema.properties)` against `Object.keys(json.properties)` read from `schema/v1.json`. With this change, `tsProps` gains `provenance` while `jsonProps` does not, so this test will fail.

Secondary, lower-severity gap: the hand-authored TypeScript interfaces `WorkspaceJsonV3`/`WorkspaceJsonV4` in `packages/spec/src/types.ts:66-101,245-279` were also not updated to include `provenance`, so even once the schema files are reconciled, statically-typed consumers have no compile-time way to read/write the new field (both interfaces lack a top-level index signature, unlike their nested `manual`/`generated` members).

## FILES INSPECTED
- `packages/spec/src/schema.ts` (full file, and via diff) — confirmed `provenance` was added only here, as a sibling of `manual`/`generated`/`agents`/`health` under the strict (`additionalProperties: false`) top-level `properties`.
- `packages/spec/schema/v1.json` (tail) — confirmed no `provenance` key exists; last top-level property is `health`.
- `packages/spec/src/index.ts` — confirmed `validate()`/`validateV4()` compile and use `schema/v1.json` (not `schema.ts`'s `workspaceJsonSchema`) as the actual runtime validation source.
- `packages/spec/src/validator.ts` — confirmed `compileSchemaValidator` uses Ajv with `strict: false` against whatever schema object it's given (no independent evidence of a bug here, just confirming Ajv setup).
- `packages/spec/src/types.ts` — confirmed `WorkspaceJsonV3`/`WorkspaceJsonV4` have no `provenance` field and no top-level index signature.
- `packages/spec/src/index.test.ts` (lines ~1-40, 270-360) — confirmed an existing "no split-brain" test (`workspaceJsonSchema top-level property keys match schema/v1.json`, lines 324-329) that this diff will cause to fail.
- `packages/spec/package.json` — confirmed the `build`/`test` scripts (`tsc`, then `vitest run`) do not regenerate `schema/v1.json` from `schema.ts`, so nothing in the build pipeline would auto-sync the two files.

## Correctness problem

The diff adds a new `provenance` object to the **TypeScript schema mirror** `packages/spec/src/schema.ts:228-238`, but does not update the **packaged JSON Schema artifact** `packages/spec/schema/v1.json`, which is a separate, checked-in file.

This matters because the runtime validator does not use `workspaceJsonSchema` from `schema.ts` at all. `packages/spec/src/index.ts:37-42` loads and compiles `../schema/v1.json` from disk — the comment there states explicitly: *"The runtime validator consumes the schema artifact that is published with the package, rather than the authoring-time TypeScript mirror."* I confirmed `schema/v1.json` (tail read) still ends with `health` as the last top-level property and has no `provenance` key, and the top-level schema keeps `additionalProperties: false` (mirrored at `packages/spec/src/schema.ts:7`, and asserted by test at `packages/spec/src/index.test.ts:331-333`).

Consequence: any document that actually includes a `provenance` field will be **rejected** by `validate()`/`validateV4()` at runtime (additional-property violation against the strict top-level schema in `v1.json`), even though the diff's intent — and the exported `workspaceJsonSchema` TS constant — says `provenance` is a valid optional field. The two schema sources are now out of sync ("split-brain").

This is not just a theoretical risk: the repo has an explicit regression test guarding exactly this invariant, `packages/spec/src/index.test.ts:324-329` ("workspaceJsonSchema top-level property keys match schema/v1.json"), which diffs `Object.keys(workspaceJsonSchema.properties)` against `Object.keys(json.properties)` read from `schema/v1.json`. With this change, `tsProps` gains `provenance` while `jsonProps` does not, so this test will fail.

Secondary, lower-severity gap: the hand-authored TypeScript interfaces `WorkspaceJsonV3`/`WorkspaceJsonV4` in `packages/spec/src/types.ts:66-101,245-279` were also not updated to include `provenance`, so even once the schema files are reconciled, statically-typed consumers have no compile-time way to read/write the new field (both interfaces lack a top-level index signature, unlike their nested `manual`/`generated` members).

## FILES INSPECTED
- `packages/spec/src/schema.ts` (full file, and via diff) — confirmed `provenance` was added only here, as a sibling of `manual`/`generated`/`agents`/`health` under the strict (`additionalProperties: false`) top-level `properties`.
- `packages/spec/schema/v1.json` (tail) — confirmed no `provenance` key exists; last top-level property is `health`.
- `packages/spec/src/index.ts` — confirmed `validate()`/`validateV4()` compile and use `schema/v1.json` (not `schema.ts`'s `workspaceJsonSchema`) as the actual runtime validation source.
- `packages/spec/src/validator.ts` — confirmed `compileSchemaValidator` uses Ajv with `strict: false` against whatever schema object it's given (no independent evidence of a bug here, just confirming Ajv setup).
- `packages/spec/src/types.ts` — confirmed `WorkspaceJsonV3`/`WorkspaceJsonV4` have no `provenance` field and no top-level index signature.
- `packages/spec/src/index.test.ts` (lines ~1-40, 270-360) — confirmed an existing "no split-brain" test (`workspaceJsonSchema top-level property keys match schema/v1.json`, lines 324-329) that this diff will cause to fail.
- `packages/spec/package.json` — confirmed the `build`/`test` scripts (`tsc`, then `vitest run`) do not regenerate `schema/v1.json` from `schema.ts`, so nothing in the build pipeline would auto-sync the two files.
